At some point you have to ask what the fuck the point of maximizing the number is.

If I die with $5m, I didn't "win."

I spent 40 years turning time into money just so someone else could inherit the money after I turned into dirt.

The optimal wealth curve for me isn't:

«accumulate retire preserve die rich»

It's:

«accumulate reach FU money gradually convert money back into life die with ~$0»

And "die with zero" doesn't literally mean $0.00 in the checking account at 11:59 PM.

It means don't spend your whole life optimizing for a balance sheet that has no use after you're gone.

A dollar has wildly different utility depending on when you spend it.

$100k at 30 can buy freedom.

$100k at 50 can buy time.

$100k at 80 might buy absolutely fucking nothing because you're too old to do the things you wanted to do with it.

So maybe the real financial optimization problem isn't:

maximize terminal wealth

It's:

maximize lifetime utility subject to not running out of money.

Once you have enough, the goal of investing should arguably change from accumulation to decumulation.

Not "how do I get to $10m?"

More like:

"How much of this can I turn into a better life while I'm still alive?"

The weirdest form of poverty is dying with a huge portfolio because you were too afraid to use it.
